newsitem.title: GERMANY: Weak mark makes German labour more competitive - IW.
newsitem.headline: Weak mark makes German labour more competitive - IW.

text.p: The mark's recent weakness will show its upside this year, by lowering west German labour costs relative to international competitors, the IW economic research institute said on Wednesday.

Preliminary studies show west German unit-wage costs should be 0.2 percent lower in 1997 than in 1995, while similar costs for other major industrial nations will show a nine percent rise when calculated in marks, the institute said.
This should help make exports -- already Germany's economic bright spot -- more competitive, IW said. The dollar's current level of 1.73 marks is up from 1.35 marks two years ago.
But German unit-labour costs would have to fall another 12 percent to restore the relationships that prevailed in 1989, prior to German reunification, IW said.

German exporters lost one fifth of their world market share in the first half of the decade as the strong mark boosted German unit labour costs by 20 percent relative to its 11 most important foreign competitors, it said.

The study projected west German unit wage costs at 148.5 in 1997, compared with a base of 100 in 1980. The other 11 countries' unit-wage costs were seen at 132.7 when calculated in marks, and at 142.2 calculated in national currencies.
